raw_response:
Alright, let me think this through. I've been farming these 15 mu for 40 years now, and I know this land well. Quzhou ground is decent — a bit salty in patches but we've worked it for decades. I went through high school, so I read the fertilizer bags, I talk to the agri-tech station people, and I follow a few WeChat groups where the extension agents post.

My plan this year is mostly what I did last year, with small adjustments.

**Wheat-maize rotation — 12 mu.** This is the bread and butter here. Everyone in Quzhou does it. I'll put 12 mu into the rotation because that's what the double-crop system handles best with my well.

**Cotton — 3 mu.** Cotton prices have been weak but I keep a patch because the land on the west side is saltier and cotton tolerates it better than maize. My household is just me and my wife, so 3 mu of cotton is about what the two of us can pick without hiring much help.

For the winter wheat, I sow in early October. I use an improved variety — Jimai 22 or similar, whatever the seed dealer has that's certified. I apply about 40 kg of diammonium phosphate and 20 kg of urea as base fertilizer before sowing, then topdress with another 15 kg of urea at jointing in spring. That works out to around 16 kg of pure N per mu, 8 kg P2O5. Potassium I add maybe 6 kg K2O as compound fertilizer. I irrigate at overwintering, jointing, and grain-filling — three times. If spring is dry I add one more. I spray twice — once for aphids and powdery mildew around jointing, once for wheat midge at heading. I expect about 500 kg per mu; last year I got 510.

For the summer maize, I plant right after wheat harvest in mid-June, no-till with a seeder straight into the stubble. Hybrid seed, Zhengdan 958 type. I side-dress 25 kg urea at big-trumpet stage, plus I broadcast 30 kg compound before sowing. About 17 kg N, 6 kg P, 6 kg K per mu. One irrigation usually, unless drought hits — then two. One pesticide spray for corn borer. Expect 550 kg per mu.

For cotton, I sow in late April under film. I use a Bt variety — saves me pesticide sprays on bollworm. Base fertilizer 30 kg compound plus 15 kg urea at flowering, another 10 kg at boll-setting. About 14 kg N, 7 kg P, 9 kg K per mu — cotton needs more potassium for the bolls. Irrigate twice. Still need 4 sprays for aphids, spider mites, and blight even with Bt. Expect 280 kg seed cotton per mu.

I'd rather put on a little extra urea than come up short — a weak crop costs me far more than a bag of fertilizer.
